title: Metric census, trace boundaries, and query-budget playbook
content:
Purpose:
- Create a compact, actionable playbook that binds the metric census (what metrics we collect and why) to concrete trace-boundary rules and query budget guidance for dashboards and alerting.
- Focus: inference runtime (token-serving), routing/fallbacks, and cache/batching components.

Scope and intended audience:
- Observability engineers, SREs, serving-runtime owners, and dashboard authors.
- This is not a complete instrumentation spec for user-facing product metrics; it is targeted to runtime telemetry and cost-aware dashboards.

High-level goals:
- Reduce query cost by 30% for the top 10 operational dashboards within 90 days via census + sampling + query budget fixes.
- Standardize trace boundaries so debugging latency regressions requires <= 2 drilldowns.
- Surface high-cardinality signals only behind on-demand widgets or rollup views.

Definitions / quick glossary:
- Metric census: authoritative list of metrics, owners, cardinality expectations, retention, and why we keep them.
- Trace boundary: where a span starts and ends for a logical operation (e.g., user request -> model invocation -> token generation -> response).
- Query budget: per-dashboard/slo TTL and cost target (tokens/row-read/compute cost).

Metric census: recommended canonical fields (for each metric row in the census)
- metric_name: short (snake_case).
- owner: team or individual.
- intent: alerting | dashboard | experiment | perf-regression.
- cardinality: low | medium | high (with example cardinalities).
- aggregation: sum | count | p50/p90 | max | histogram-buckets.
- retention_target: 7d | 30d | 90d | 13mo.
- sample_strategy: none | rate-based | head-only | tail-only | reservoir.
- cost_impact_notes: short note estimating query cost risk.

Example census entries (informal):
- inference.request.latency_ms, owner: eng-serving-runtime, intent: sla, cardinality: low, aggregation: p50/p90/p99, retention: 90d, sample_strategy: none, cost_impact_notes: primary SLI; keep full.
- kv_cache.hit_rate, owner: eng-serving-runtime, intent: perf-debug, cardinality: medium (shard_id), aggregation: p95, retention: 30d, sample_strategy: rate-based 10%, cost_impact_notes: shard-level high-card — aggregate by region for dashboards.
- model.variant.cpu_seconds, owner: infra, intent: cost, cardinality: medium, aggregation: sum, retention: 90d, sample_strategy: none, cost_impact_notes: used for billing reconciliation.
- request.prompt_length_tokens, owner: product-hosted-api, intent: billing/dash, cardinality: high (customer_id), aggregation: histogram, retention: 30d, sample_strategy: head-only 1% + rolling tail reservoir 1000/day, cost_impact_notes: very high cardinality — avoid raw customer_id on global dashboards.

Trace boundary conventions (practical rules):
- Global rule: prefer coarse-grained top-level spans for user-visible latencies, and optional fine-grained nested spans for heavy internal subsystems (batching, KV cache, kernel).
- Top-level span name: request:{api,route,model} with standard tags: request_id, customer_id(hash), route, model_version, deployment_id.
- Internal spans: start only when their latency routinely exceeds 5% of top-level p95 OR when their internal errors exceed threshold. Avoid instrumenting every micro-op by default.
- Batching boundaries: each batch invocation must have a span with batch_size and contributed_request_ids (or a hash). Do not expand contributed_request_ids in traces sent to public tracing backend—use a separate small mapping store for heavyweight reconstruction.
- KV cache: create two spans: kv.lookup (fast) and kv.load_if_miss (longer). Tag misses with miss_reason to help identify transient capacity/serialization issues.
- Fallback flows: always create a short span indicating fallback decision and reason (e.g., capacity-signal, model-degraded, routing-error). This is invaluable for rollback RCA.

Trace sampling heuristics and budget:
- Default: adaptive sampling that keeps 1% of all traces for full payload, but boosts to 100% for traces with status!=ok, latency>p99, or fallback events.
- Reservoir per-route: maintain a 1k/day reservoir of tail traces per critical route (hosted-api inference routes).
- Priority sampling: traces that include new rollout model versions (flagged by model_version tag matching canary range) should be oversampled for 24–72 hours post roll.
- Privacy: redact phi and PII at instrumentation layer; do not include raw prompt text in traces in primary tracing backend—store a pointer to ephemeral object (S3) accessible only to authorized investigators.

Dashboard guidance and query-budget rules:
- Single-panel rule: queries that touch high-cardinality metric dimensions must either aggregate to a precomputed rollup or be guarded by a 30s max-rows limit.
- Widget types: prefer sparklines/summary numbers for high-cardinality signals, and make a drilldown widget for heavy queries (marked with a badge "heavy").
- Default time window on dashboards: 1h for operational, 24h for cost/capacity views. Avoid default 30d unless explicitly required.
- Refresh frequency: operational dashboards 15s–60s depending on importance; business dashboards 5m–1h. Ensure the query budget setting in dashboard meta matches the expected refresh cadence.
- Query budget meta: store and publish expected query cost per widget (low|medium|high) and a daily budget for each dashboard owner. Exceeding budget triggers automated email to owner and throttled refresh.

Concrete dashboard changes to make now (quick wins):
- Replace raw customer_id grouped panels with hashed_customer_id rollups + sample percent to show distribution; provide a drilldown link that runs with a guarded query.
- Convert 3 heavy 'top N' panels to precomputed views updated every 5m (small Spark job).
- Add a visual "query cost" gauge on each dashboard header showing current spend vs daily budget.

Alerting and SLO ties:
- Each alert that relies on a high-cardinality metric needs an explicit fallback metric that is low-cardinality (e.g., per-region or global error_rate).
- SLOs: use user-experienced latency p95/p99 (top-level spans). Create secondary SLOs for internal subsystems (cache_miss_rate, batching_latency_p95).

Instrumenter checklist (low friction):
- instrumenter adds metric to local census draft (PR template: metric + owner + intent + cardinality estimate).
- run a query-cost estimate script (internal tool) to get expected cost for 7d and 30d windows.
- if high-cost, pick a sampling strategy or rollup and document in census entry.
- include unit test that asserts tags included (request_id, hashed_customer_id, model_version).

Implementation notes / anti-patterns observed:
- Avoid adding customer_id as a free-form tag on high-cardinality metrics—this has caused runaway query cost in dashboards. Use hashed or bucketing strategies.
- Too many spans on every request: we saw x3 trace volume spike when ops instrumented every kernel call. Add instrumentation gate: only instrument an internal span if the op is expected to be >10ms or it fails.
- Dashboard "copy-and-paste" queries with different time windows lead to 6x query duplication; prefer dashboard variable-driven queries and a single canonical query per metric.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- How do we integrate ephemeral prompt payload storage with ROPs audit requirements? Decision owner: security-compliance (see CONFLUENCE:OBS-PRIVACY-3).
- Should we create a "heavy-query" enforcement layer in the dashboard service that blocks refreshes above budget? Quick experiment: prototype with 2 dashboards. Owner: eng-observability.
- Retention policy: do we keep histogram buckets for prompt_length_tokens beyond 30d for cost analysis? Owner: product-hosted-api.

Next steps / action items (first 30 days):
- (Ava) Draft the canonical metric census spreadsheet and PR template (due 1/20).
- (Jordan) Implement guarded drilldown link pattern and prototype cost gauge on one alerting dashboard (due 1/28).
- (Priya) Add adaptive trace sampling knobs to the tracer and test with reservoir limits (due 2/03).
- (Mateo) Run query-cost audit for top 20 dashboards and rank candidates for conversion to rollups (due 2/07).

Notes-to-self / informal brainstorm fragments:
- Might be worth a "cost tier" label on dashboards so sales/ops know which are on low/medium/high cost budgets.
- Could we export a daily "dashboard burn" CSV to billing and alert owners if their widgets spike?
- Slack-runbook: add a quick command to request a heavy trace dump for a request_id (obs-trace dump <id>) that temporarily lifts sampling gate for that id only.

References and links:
- CONFLUENCE:OBS-INSTR-101 (instrumentation standards)
- JIRA:OBS-1324 (rollout oversampling work)
- GITHUB:repo/obs-instrumentation#248 (sampling implementation PR)
- Slack: #obs-instrumentation (discussion thread around query budgets)

Status: draft — this is intentionally practical and lightweight. Will iterate after 1st implementation sprint and incorporate measurement data from the audit.

Unresolved: confirm retention limits with finance for cost allocation (Finance owner: TBA).

End of playbook (working draft).
